question: How can a multi-agent system retrieve both facts and procedural instructions (style/structure) from a vector store instead of simulated data?
contributions: Dual RAG architecture: a KnowledgeStore namespace for facts and a ContextLibrary namespace for semantic blueprints in one Pinecone index
A Context Librarian agent that retrieves a blueprint by intent
An Orchestrator that splits a goal into intent_query and topic_query

limits: No measurement of retrieval quality, latency or cost; the corpus is 2 chunks and 3 blueprints.
The author notes clearing namespaces every run is for teaching only; chunk size and overlap must be tuned per data type.
Model choice gpt-5 is for continuity; the chapter says the engine is model-agnostic. No score threshold on retrieval is described.
practices: Keep facts and procedural instructions in separate namespaces so either can be updated independently (Architecting a dual RAG MAS).
Embed only the blueprint description and store the full JSON in metadata (Data preparation: context library).
Use the same embedding model for indexing and retrieval (Installation and setup).
Chunk by token count with overlap rather than characters (Helper functions).
Wait for an asynchronous namespace delete to finish before upserting (Initializing the Pinecone index).
Provide a default blueprint fallback and halt gracefully on invalid orchestrator JSON (Librarian, Orchestrator sections).
